Simulate a table from a profile

Source: R/simulate_from_profile.R
simulate_from_profile.Rd

Draws n synthetic rows from a csdb_profile. The rows follow the published summaries and hold no row of the profiled data.

Usage

simulate_from_profile(profile, n = 1000L, seed = 1L, world = NULL)

Arguments

profile

A csdb_profile, from profile_query(), read_profile() or profile_schema().

n

The number of rows, a whole number of at least 1. NULL gives 1000 rows, the default.

seed

The seed for set.seed(). The function restores the random state of the caller on exit.

world

NULL, or a named list that maps a column to its allowed values. The function converts the values to the column's type. It ignores, without a message, each element that names no column of profile$field_types, so one world can serve several tables.

Value

A data.table with n rows and the columns of profile$field_types, in that order.

Details

The R type of each column follows its field type: TEXT character, INTEGER integer, DOUBLE double, BOOLEAN logical, DATE Date and DATETIME POSIXct in UTC.

A column takes its values from its own summary:

  • levels or days: a draw of the published values, weighted by n. The suppressed cells generate nothing. A DATETIME drawn from days gets a uniform whole second within its UTC day.

  • weeks, months or quarters: a cell drawn by n, then a uniform day within it. A cell of quarters ends with the quarter in quarters_to when the profile holds quarters_to.

  • breaks: a bin drawn by n, then a uniform value within the bin. An INTEGER value is a uniform whole number within the bin. A column with nonnegative TRUE draws no value below 0.

  • n_distinct of a TEXT column: "<column>_<i>", with i uniform in 1 to n_distinct.

  • missing_share: NA at that rate. A share of "suppressed" gives no NA. A key column gets no NA.

A schema_only or exclude column, and a column whose summary has no published cell, gets schema values. A TEXT or INTEGER key column gets "<column>_<i>" or i for row i, so a single-column key is unique at any n. Other columns get schema values by type:

  • TEXT: "<column>_<i>", with i from 1 to 10.

  • INTEGER: a whole number from 0 to 100.

  • DOUBLE: a uniform value from 0 to 1.

  • BOOLEAN: TRUE or FALSE. A BOOLEAN with n_distinct only also gets these values.

  • DATE and DATETIME: a uniform day from 2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31. A DATETIME gets a uniform whole second within that day.

The joint structure comes after the columns, in this order:

  1. Each crosstab draws its two columns jointly by the cell counts. This replaces the values of both columns.

  2. Each group size draws a range by n, then a uniform row count from size_from to size_to. The last range has no size_to and draws up to 2 * size_from. It draws row counts until they cover all rows, gives each group a fresh identifier, and truncates the last group. With no published range, each group has 1 row.

  3. Each dependency that holds gives every value of its first column one value of the second column. The function assigns the values of the first column from the most rows to the fewest. Each goes to the value of the second column that is furthest below its drawn row count. This keeps the drawn frequencies of the second column close.

Before it draws, the function computes the key space. That is the product, over the key columns, of the number of values each column can take. When n is larger, it stops with an error that names the keys, the key space and n. A key column can take:

  • a world column: its allowed values.

  • levels or days: the values with a count above 0. A DATETIME from days can take every second of those days.

  • weeks, months or quarters: every day of the cells with a count above 0. A DATETIME can take every second of those days.

  • breaks: an INTEGER takes every whole number of the bins with a count above 0, from 0 up when nonnegative is TRUE. A DOUBLE has no limit.

  • n_distinct of a TEXT column: n_distinct values.

  • a group-size column: no limit, because each group gets a fresh identifier.

  • schema values: no limit for a TEXT, INTEGER or DOUBLE key column, and 2 for BOOLEAN. A DATE takes the 1827 days from 2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31, and a DATETIME every second of those days.

A crosstab replaces its columns, so a key column of a crosstab can take the values that it has in the cells left after world. The key space does not count crosstab pairs or dependencies, so it is an upper bound.

The function redraws each row whose keys repeat an earlier row. After 20 redraws it stops with an error that names the keys and n. A redrawn row keeps the values of its group-size columns.

A world column takes its values from world only. A value that the column's levels or days also hold keeps its published weight. Every other value gets the mean of those weights, or all values get equal weights when the profile holds none of them. A crosstab keeps only the cells whose values world allows, and has no effect when no cell is left. A group-size column takes its identifiers from world, without replacement where world has enough values.

See also

Other simulation functions: profile_compare(), profile_schema()

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  sex = rep(c("female", "male"), 10),
  age = rep(c(4L, 15L, 38L, 52L, 71L), 4)
)
p <- profile_data(
  d,
  c(sex = "TEXT", age = "INTEGER"),
  columns = c(sex = "full", age = "coarsen")
)
simulate_from_profile(p, n = 5, seed = 2)
#>       sex   age
#>    <char> <int>
#> 1:   male    11
#> 2: female    33
#> 3: female    15
#> 4:   male    29
#> 5: female    42
